brief_title: PDE-4 Inhibitor Roflumilast and GLP-1 Agonist Liraglutide in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
official_title: Short-term Treatment With PDE-4 Inhibitor Roflumilast or GLP-1 Agonist Liraglutide or Metformin in Treatment Naive Obese Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome

primary_outcomes.measure: The main outcome was change in body weight.
primary_outcomes.time_frame: Patient's body weight was mesured at the base point and every four weeks during 12 weeks of clinical trial.

brief_summary: The purpose of this study was to determine whether monotherapy treatment with phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE-4) inhibitor roflumilast is more effective than treatment with glucagon-like protein 1 (GLP-1) liraglutide or treatment with metformin as monotherapy in the treatment of obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) regarding weight reduction who have not been treated before. The investigators anticipated greater changes in body weight in patients on roflumilast treatment than in liraglutide or metformin.

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* 18 years old to menopause
* polycystic ovary syndrome (NICHD criteria)
* BMI of 30 kg/m² or higher

Exclusion Criteria:

* depression
* type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus
* history of carcinoma
* history of pancreatitis
* Cushing's syndrome or congenital (non-classic) adrenal hyperplasia
* significant cardiovascular, kidney or hepatic disease
* the use of medications other than metformin known or suspected to affect reproductive or metabolic functions
* the use of statins, within 90 days prior to study entry
